test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 28 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Nalanda University is widely recognised as one of the ancient world's great universities and an important Buddhist centre of academic excellence. Which Indian ruler founded it?
solution:
The correct answer is __**kumargupta I**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kumargupta I** was an **emperor of the Gupta Empire of Ancient India**.
 
• He was the **Gupta emperor Chandragupta II and queen Dhruvadevi **
 
 
• **he appears to have kept control of the land he inherited which extended from gujarat in the west to the bengal region in the east **
 
 
 
• **The Nalanda monastery university was founded by kumargupta I, according to numeristic evidence uncovered at Nalanda.**
 
• **Nalanda was an acclaimed Mahavihara, a large Buddhist monastery in the ancient kingdom of Magadha (modern-day Bihar) in India**.
 
• **from the fifth century CE to 1200 CE **the location which lies** 95 kilometers southeast of patna close to the town of bihar sharif, served as a centre of learning.**
 
 
• **It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashoka was an Indian emperor of the Maurya empire son of bindusara**

 
 
• ​**​**He was remembered as a **model king who governed a huge and diverse mauryan kingdom with dharma at the core of this worldview.**
 
 
 
• **Chandragupta** was the **founder of the Mauryan dynasty ****and the first emperor to unify most of India under one administration**.
 
 
• He is regarded with rescuing the nation from poor leadership and liberating it from foreign hegemony.
 
 
 
• ​**Harshavardhana was an Indian emperor who ruled northern India**
 
 
• **​**He belonged to the** Pushyabhuti also called the Vardhana dynasty**.
 
• He was a Hindu who later **embraced Mahayana Buddhism.**
 
 

43:T13
